question: What best describes a pathogen?

options.A: Any living organism in the environment
options.B: A harmless commensal bacteria in the gut
options.C: A microbe capable of causing disease
options.D: A microorganism used to produce antibiotics

explanation: You've got this! A pathogen is simply any germ—like a bacterium or virus—that can invade the body and make a person sick. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h1)

question: When do opportunistic pathogens usually cause trouble?

options.A: When the host immune system is weakened
options.B: Directly after a standard surgical procedure
options.C: During high exposure in a sterile laboratory
options.D: When a patient takes broad-spectrum vitamins

explanation: Think of opportunists as bullies—they wait until the body's natural defenses are down, like when someone is very sick or tired, before they attack. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which type of microorganism lacks a true nucleus?
explanation: Spot on! Prokaryotes (like bacteria) are simple cells that keep their genetic material floating freely without a neat membrane-bound nucleus. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why are viruses kept in a totally different category from bacteria and fungi?

options.A: They can replicate independently on inanimate surfaces
options.B: They possess complex eukaryotic cellular machinery
options.C: They are visible to the naked eye under sunlight
options.D: They are non-cellular agents requiring a host

explanation: Viruses aren't even fully living cells on their own! They can't reproduce unless they hijack a living host cell. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h2)

question: What shape is a bacterial cell called a coccus?
explanation: Easy peasy! 'Coccus' sounds round, and these bacteria are indeed shaped like little spheres. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why do Gram-negative bacteria turn pink during a Gram stain?

options.A: They produce natural pigments that react with iodine
options.B: They lack any form of cellular wall structure
options.C: They have a thin peptidoglycan wall and outer membrane
options.D: They absorb excessive amounts of crystal violet dye

explanation: Because their cell wall is thin, the first purple stain washes right out, leaving them ready to soak up the pink counterstain. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the protective protein coat around a virus's genetic material called?
explanation: Think of the capsid as a sturdy little armor shell that protects the virus's inner secrets. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h4)

question: What do we call a virus that specifically targets and infects bacteria?
explanation: Bacteriophages are basically bacteria-eaters! They are specialized viruses that hunt down and destroy bacterial cells. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h4)

question: What are the thread-like branching structures that make up molds called?
explanation: Hyphae are tiny, thread-like filaments that grow and tangle together to form the fuzzy structure of molds. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h5)

question: What term describes an insect that carries a germ from one person to another?
explanation: Think of a vector as a biological taxi—like a mosquito carrying the malaria parasite straight to a human host. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which process completely destroys ALL microbial life, including tough spores?
explanation: Sterilization is the ultimate clean! Nothing survives it—not even stubborn bacterial spores. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h6)

question: What do we call chemical agents safe to apply to living skin to kill germs?
explanation: Antiseptics (like spirit or iodine) are gentle enough for human skin, unlike harsh disinfectants meant for hospital floors. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why do laboratories run antimicrobial sensitivity tests?

options.A: To sterilize medical equipment using chemical agents
options.B: To find which drugs are effective against a pathogen
options.C: To count the exact number of human cells in blood
options.D: To determine the viral load of an infected patient

explanation: This test helps doctors figure out which specific antibiotic will actually knock out the patient's infection. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why is empiric antibiotic therapy often started before lab culture results come back?

options.A: To eliminate the need for taking laboratory specimens
options.B: To prevent the development of drug-resistant spores
options.C: To provide immediate treatment for severe infections
options.D: To ensure the patient has a sterile bloodstream

explanation: We can't always wait days for lab results when a patient is very sick. Doctors use educated guesses (empiric therapy) to start treatment right away! [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h7)
